protocol.source_text:
Animal / Mammalian Bites
General wound care
Wash thoroughly with large volume water + soap
Specific bite management
Extensive high pressure irrigation
Assess wound + rabies risk – refer to Rabies PEP protocol
Vaccination status: ATT booster if required
High risk wounds
Controversies of suturing
Suturing for haemostasis is required
Local anaesthetic given from inside wound
Suturing for cosmesis (eg. face) is acceptable – may require referral to Plastics
If wound < 8 hours + thoroughly cleaned, may be sutured – ideally loose sutures,
just opposing edges that will allow for swelling
If wound > 8 hours: avoid suturing + L/A
 
Debridement
Of devitalized tissue (especially jagged wounds) 
Antibiotic prophylaxis
Risk of infection related to risk factors, site  + type of bites > cat > dogs
Antibiotic prophylaxis will depend on risk
Polymicrobial infections
Discharge advice
Health education about appropriate wound care 
Signs of infection, cellulitis, sepsis + danger signs
Strict instructions to return if any concerns
Wound factors
Patient factors
Extensive contamination
Immunocompromised
Crush with devitalized tissue
Malnourished
Puncture
Diabetes melliitis
Bites to hands, wrist, feet + face, genitalia
Haem-oncology 
Wounds that penetrate bone, joints, tendons + 
neurovascular structures
Post-splenectomy
Delayed presentation > 8 hrs
Autoimmune disease
RMMCH EM Clinical Protocols V5 03/01/2024
